questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which reagent selectively reduces an acid chloride ($\text{RCOCl}$) to an aldehyde ($\text{RCHO}$) without further reduction to the primary alcohol?
questions.explanationEn: Lithium tri-*tert*-butoxyaluminium hydride, $\text{LiAlH(O}t\text{-Bu)}_3$, is a sterically bulky, attenuated hydride donor that selectively reduces highly reactive acid chlorides to aldehydes at $-78\,^\circ\text{C}$ without over-reducing the aldehyde to an alcohol. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following carbocations, the most stable species is
questions.explanationEn: The tropylium cation ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7^+$) is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and contains $6\,\pi$ electrons, satisfying Hückel's $(4n+2)\,\pi$ rule for aromaticity. This aromatic stabilization makes it substantially more stable than benzyl, *tert*-butyl, and allyl carbocations. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which organometallic reagent converts propanoyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCl}$) cleanly to pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) without further addition to a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanationEn: Lithium dialkylcuprates (Gilman reagents, $\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$) are soft, mildly nucleophilic organometallic reagents that react rapidly with acid chlorides to form ketones, but do not undergo 1,2-addition to the resulting ketone. Thus $\text{Et}_2\text{CuLi}$ cleanly gives pentan-3-one. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Thermal decomposition of an acyl azide ($\text{RCON}_3$) in dry toluene followed by hydrolysis with water to yield a primary amine ($\text{RNH}_2$) with one fewer carbon atom is known as the
questions.explanationEn: Thermal loss of $\text{N}_2$ from an acyl azide ($\text{RCON}_3$) with concerted 1,2-migration of $\text{R}$ to nitrogen gives an isocyanate ($\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O}$), which hydrolyzes to $\text{RNH}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$. This is the **Curtius rearrangement**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of $(R)$-butan-2-ol with thionyl chloride ($\text{SOCl}_2$) in neat dioxane (without pyridine) predominantly yields
questions.explanationEn: In the absence of a base such as pyridine, reaction of a chiral secondary alcohol with $\text{SOCl}_2$ proceeds through a chlorosulfite intermediate ($\text{ROSOCl}$) that collapses via an intimate ion pair (internal nucleophilic substitution, $\text{S}_\text{N}i$). Chloride is delivered from the same face as the departing $-\text{OSOCl}$ group, giving net **retention of configuration**, i.e., $(R)$-2-chlorobutane. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of $(1R,2R)$-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylpropane with $\text{NaOEt}$ in $\text{EtOH}$ proceeds via a stereospecific E2 mechanism to afford predominantly
questions.explanationEn:
Let us determine the anti-periplanar E2 stereochemistry of $(1R,2R)$-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylpropane:
1. At C1 ($1R$; priorities: $-\text{Br} > -\text{CH(Ph)Me} > -\text{Ph} > -\text{H}$): placing $-\text{Br}$ down (in-plane) puts $-\text{Ph}$ front-right (wedge) and $-\text{H}$ back-left (dash).
2. At C2 ($2R$; priorities: $-\text{CH(Br)Ph} > -\text{Ph} > -\text{Me} > -\text{H}$): rotating so $-\text{H}$ is up (anti-periplanar to $-\text{Br}$) places $-\text{Ph}$ front-right (wedge) and $-\text{Me}$ back-left (dash).
3. Eliminating $\text{H}$ and $\text{Br}$ leaves the two $-\text{Ph}$ groups on the **same side** of the $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ bond. Since $-\text{Ph} > -\text{H}$ at C1 and $-\text{Ph} > -\text{Me}$ at C2, the alkene is **$(Z)$-1,2-diphenylprop-1-ene**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which transformation is best accomplished using Wolff–Kishner reduction ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2, \text{KOH}, \text{diethylene glycol}, \Delta$) rather than Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl}$)?
questions.explanationEn: The **Wolff–Kishner reduction** operates under strongly **basic** conditions, which preserve acid-sensitive protecting groups such as **acetals (1,3-dioxolanes)** that would rapidly hydrolyze under strongly acidic Clemmensen conditions. Conversely, esters (C) would saponify and primary alkyl bromides (D) would undergo elimination/substitution under hot $\text{KOH}$. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Reduction of $(E)$-but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde) with $\text{NaBH}_4$ in the presence of $\text{CeCl}_3\cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in methanol (Luche reduction) gives predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Under **Luche reduction** conditions ($\text{NaBH}_4/\text{CeCl}_3$ in $\text{MeOH}$), hard Lewis-acidic $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ coordinates to the carbonyl oxygen and converts $\text{BH}_4^-$ into harder alkoxyborohydrides, strongly favoring **1,2-reduction** of $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyls to allylic alcohols without conjugate 1,4-reduction. Thus $(E)$-but-2-enal gives **$(E)$-but-2-en-1-ol**. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide ($\text{Et}-\text{S}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$) is hydrolyzed in aqueous ethanol, it reacts over $10^4$ times faster than 1-chlorobutane. If the $\text{C1}$ carbon (bonded to $\text{Cl}$) is isotopically labeled as $^{13}\text{C}$, the hydrolyzed alcohol product is
questions.explanationEn: The sulfur lone pair intramolecularly displaces $\text{Cl}^-$ via neighboring group participation to form a **symmetrical cyclic episulfonium ion** ($\text{Et}-\text{S}^+(\text{CH}_2-^{13}\text{CH}_2)$). Water then opens this symmetrical three-membered ring with equal probability at either ring carbon, producing a **$1:1$ mixture** of the two isotopomeric alcohols. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Photochemical ($h\nu$) electrocyclic ring closure of $(2E,4Z)$-hexa-2,4-diene yields
questions.explanationEn: A $4\pi$-electron electrocyclization under **photochemical ($h\nu$)** conditions is **disrotatory** (opposite to thermal conrotatory). In $(2E,4Z)$-hexa-2,4-diene, one methyl group points outward and one points inward; disrotatory closure rotates one methyl up and the other down, stereospecifically yielding ***trans*-3,4-dimethylcyclobut-1-ene**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following rearrangements proceed through an **isocyanate** ($\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O}$) intermediate?
questions.explanationEn: The **Hofmann** (from primary amides + $\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}$), **Curtius** (from acyl azides + $\Delta$), and **Lossen** (from $O$-acyl hydroxamic acids + base) rearrangements all involve concerted 1,2-migration of $\text{R}$ to electron-deficient nitrogen to generate an **isocyanate** ($\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O}$). By contrast, the **Beckmann rearrangement** proceeds through a **nitrilium ion** ($\text{R}-\text{C}^+=\text{N}-\text{R}'$) rather than an isocyanate. Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following reactions generate a carbene or carbenoid intermediate?
optionsEn: Treatment of $\text{CHCl}_3$ with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ and phase-transfer catalyst
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** $\alpha$-Elimination generates dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$).
- **(B) Correct:** Simmons–Smith reagent generates the zinc carbenoid $\text{ICH}_2\text{ZnI}$.
- **(C) Correct:** Photolysis of $\text{CH}_2\text{N}_2$ expels $\text{N}_2$ to generate methylene ($:\text{CH}_2$).
- **(D) Incorrect:** Standard $\text{S}_\text{N}2$/E2 reaction with no carbene intermediate.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pericyclic processes are **thermally allowed** according to the Woodward–Hoffmann rules?
questions.explanationEn:
Under thermal conditions:
- **(A) Allowed:** $6$ electrons ($4n+2$) $\implies$ $[4_s + 2_s]$ Diels–Alder is thermally allowed.
- **(B) Allowed:** $4\pi$ ($4n$) electrocyclic reactions are thermally **conrotatory**.
- **(C) Allowed:** $6\pi$ ($4n+2$) electrocyclic reactions are thermally **disrotatory**.
- **(D) Forbidden:** $[\pi 2_s + \pi 2_s]$ is a $4$-electron cycloaddition, which is thermally forbidden (photochemically allowed).
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about alkene dihydroxylation and cleavage is/are correct?
optionsEn: Catalytic $\text{OsO}_4$ with NMO performs stereospecific *syn*-dihydroxylation of alkenes.
Epoxidation of $(E)$-but-2-ene with $m$-CPBA followed by acid-catalyzed hydrolysis yields *meso*-butane-2,3-diol.
Treatment of $(Z)$-but-2-ene with cold dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields a racemic mixture of butane-2,3-diol.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** $\text{OsO}_4$/NMO forms a cyclic osmate ester via *syn* addition.
- **(B) Correct:** *Syn* epoxidation of $(E)$-but-2-ene gives the *trans*-epoxide; *anti* ring opening by $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+$ yields net *anti*-dihydroxylation $\implies$ ***meso*-butane-2,3-diol**.
- **(C) Incorrect:** Cold dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ performs *syn*-dihydroxylation, converting $(Z)$-but-2-ene into ***meso*-butane-2,3-diol**, not a racemate.
- **(D) Correct:** *cis*-Cyclohexane-1,2-diol forms the cyclic five-membered periodate ester much more readily than the *trans* isomer.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Acid-catalyzed dehydration of pinacol (2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol) yields pinacolone. The molecular weight of pinacolone is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: Pinacol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{O}_2$) loses $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ with a 1,2-methyl shift to form pinacolone (3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$). Molecular weight $= 6(12) + 12(1) + 16 = 100\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The minimum number of equivalents of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ required for complete conversion of $1\text{ mol}$ of dimethyl succinate ($\text{MeO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Me}$) to 2,5-dimethylhexane-2,5-diol (prior to aqueous workup) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Each ester group ($-\text{CO}_2\text{Me}$) consumes $2$ equivalents of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ to form a tertiary alkoxide. Since dimethyl succinate contains $2$ ester groups, a minimum of $2 \times 2 = \mathbf{4}$ equivalents of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ is required.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of 2-bromocycloheptan-1-one with $\text{NaOMe/MeOH}$ yields a methyl cycloalkanecarboxylate via Favorskii rearrangement. The number of carbon atoms in the carbocyclic ring of the product is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The Favorskii rearrangement of a cyclic $\alpha$-haloketone contracts the ring by one carbon atom. Thus, 2-bromocycloheptan-1-one (7-membered ring) contracts to methyl cyclohexanecarboxylate, which has a **$6$**-membered ring.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of moles of $\text{H}_2$ consumed per mole of octa-1,3-dien-6-yne during exhaustive catalytic hydrogenation over $\text{Pd/C}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Octa-1,3-dien-6-yne contains $2$ carbon–carbon double bonds (each consuming $1\text{ mol H}_2$) and $1$ carbon–carbon triple bond (consuming $2\text{ mol H}_2$). Total $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= 2 + 2 = \mathbf{4}$ moles.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of constitutionally distinct (structural) monobromoalkanes possible upon free-radical monobromination of 2-methylbutane (ignoring stereoisomers) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: 2-Methylbutane ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has **4** sets of chemically non-equivalent hydrogens: (1) the two equivalent C1/C1' methyl groups, (2) the tertiary C2-H, (3) the secondary C3-$\text{CH}_2$, and (4) the terminal C4 methyl group. Thus, **$4$** constitutional monobromo isomers are possible.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Reduction of acetophenone ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$) with $\text{NaBH}_4$ in methanol gives 1-phenylethanol ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) in $80\%$ isolated yield. The mass of acetophenone required to obtain $24.4\text{ g}$ of 1-phenylethanol is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Moles of 1-phenylethanol ($\text{MW} = 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) desired $= 24.4 / 122 = 0.200\text{ mol}$.
At $80\%$ yield, moles of acetophenone required $= 0.200 / 0.80 = 0.250\text{ mol}$.
Mass of acetophenone ($\text{MW} = 120\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) $= 0.250 \times 120 = \mathbf{30.0}\text{ g}$.
